ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: the colony's animals
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: What the colony's people want for their animals, the stories and choices that come of them, and the herd's year.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: When a herd of three or more sleeps outside, someone who loves animals may ask for a barn: animal beds or sleeping spots in one barn for most of the herd answer it.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description:
The colony's animals are part of its life in Rimfolk, not only its larder and its guard. Someone milking or taming talks to the animal in front of them, a dog falls in at its person's heels, a birth in the herd is news, and an old companion's death is grieved and remembered. Colonists who love animals ask for things that help the herd and their own animals; the council faces hard choices about them in hungry weeks and bad nights; and the herdmaster looks after the people who look after them.
The everyday parts follow the setting "Pets as companions" (People). With PokéWorld, Pokémon count as the colony's animals everywhere on this page, and have a page of their own besides. Their temperaments, their friendships, feuds and grief, and the few that speak are on the page "the animals' natures".

table.li: What | When

A word to an animal | Someone milking, shearing, taming, training, tending, feeding or roping an animal in view says something to it, and a child at leisure talks to the animal beside them. These share the once-a-day rate of everything said on screen.

At its person's heels | A pet with nothing to do, near its person, follows them about for a while (not one roped, penned or at work). Its person is the one it is bonded to, its master, or else the one it is fond of: its card says "fond of" whom.
A birth in the herd | News, with the mother's name. The colony's first is a day on the calendar.
A death | A named animal's death gets a farewell from the one who loved it, with lines of their own for an old animal that died at the end of a long life and for a Pokémon.

Talk between colonists | Two people who keep animals talk shop (some practice for both), two with bonded animals swap stories, and a child asks a keeper about the animals. Face to face, as all such moments are.
Social events | A keeper shows a child the animals (the two grow closer, and the child learns something), and someone lends a herder a hand with the herd (friendship, and practice).

Small habits | Someone who loves animals and has a herd to watch, or a child, sits out with the herd for a while by day; someone who loves animals or is bonded to a big one brushes down a horse or another big animal of theirs, a little handling practice. Both need "Small habits" on.

li.heading: Their days on the map

table.li: What | On the map
Home again | Someone back after four hours or more away (a caravan, a site): their animal runs over and nuzzles them, and they say hello to it.
At the foot of the bed | At bedtime a pet up to a big dog's size goes into its person's room and sleeps at the foot of their bed; in the morning they mention it. About every three nights.
At a meal | A pet sits at the elbow of someone eating (its own person first) and watches them eat, and they tell it no, or give it a bite. About every two days.
Play | A child with free time plays chase with an animal near them (up to a horse's size, not a large hunter): the two run about together for a while. About every day.
The herd | In the early morning a herd of two or more of one kind follows its eldest (the herd's leader, when it is one of them) out to fresh grazing in its area.

The rounds | In their free time the herdmaster, or whoever is best with animals when there is none, goes round up to five of the colony's animals, stopping to look each one over. A little handling practice.
Rain and snow | When rain or snow comes on by day, up to three pets out in it go in under a roof; in the snow the young ones play in it.
A bitter night | Below -8 °C at night, a herd out in the open lies down close together around its eldest.
Raiders | As raiders come, up to two pets (never a timid one) turn toward them and call out, and someone says where they are.
A strange sky | When the sky takes on a strange colour and the wind drops, the pets go and keep close to their people for a while, and one cries out.
A death | When its person dies, an animal goes to lie by the body (or the grave it is in) and cries.

li.after: None of it sends a letter or a message, and nobody is hurt. What each did lately shows on its card. The setting "Animals' moments on the map" (How much happens) sets the pace, as for their temperaments. What is said comes as it is seen: the hello as the animal reaches its person, the word at a meal as it sits down. Fifteen of the animals' encounters now happen on the map before they are told (a welcome, the foot of the bed, a bite at a meal, a child at play, an animal following someone or keeping them company when they are low, a trick, a raid on the stores, sitting with it a while, a grudge, an old animal walking over slowly, a mother lying by her newborns, an animal standing between someone and a stranger, a cry in the night), each told as it is seen and only when what it speaks of is there, and the animals' personal stories have a step on the map at each stage.

li.heading: The herdmaster
li.text: With "Systems talk to each other" on, the herdmaster goes down to the pens within the day to give each newborn a name, if it has none. When someone's animal is sick or hurt, the herdmaster finds them in their free time and tells them how it's doing, face to face: their strain eases a little and the two grow a little closer. About once a week, someone keen on animals who is four levels or more behind the herdmaster is taken along for the day's work, a lesson on the map. Besides, as before, the herdmaster sits with anyone whose named animal dies and minds the animals of those away, and goes round the animals in their free time (the rounds, above).

li.heading: Wishes

table.li: Wish | Who asks | Granted

An animal of my own | A grown colonist who loves animals (a passion, a kind soul, a lonely one) and has none, when one of the colony's grown animals has no master. Promised, they're made its master. | +3 mood for 6 days

A barn for the herd | Someone who loves animals, the herdmaster or a kind soul, when the colony's herd of 3 or more sleeps out (likelier in the cold seasons). Fulfilled when one barn has animal beds or sleeping spots for most of the herd, from 2 to 6. | Some contentment and a journal line, no mood

Something to ride | Only with Giddy-Up 2: a hunter, a restless soul or someone who loves animals, with no mount of their own. A rideable animal of the colony's with no master is made theirs when promised; otherwise one is tamed for them. | +3 for 5 days

A favourite kind of animal | Someone fond of animals (a passion, an animal lover, a child, a kind or lonely soul) has always loved one kind: one of those this land has, or that is roaming the map, that the colony's best handler has the skill to tame. The same person keeps the same favourite while the land's animals stay the same. Promised, a calm one out there is marked for taming. With PokéWorld, a favourite Pokémon the same way, caught in a ball. | Fulfilled when the colony has one: joy, a feeling and a journal line, no mood. If it bonds to them later (while the council's promise is watched), a second moment: "it chose me"

A pack animal of my own | A hauler (hauling first in their work), someone with a passion for talk and trade, or a restless soul, with no pack animal of their own, where the colony has one with no master or the land has pack animals it could tame. Promised, the colony's spare one answers to them, else a calm wild one is marked for taming. | Some handling practice and contentment, no mood

li.after: Nobody whose ideoligion abhors bonding with animals asks for these, and nobody whose ideoligion frowns on ranching asks for a barn.

table.li: Goal | For | Done when
A champion at my side | Someone who can fight, with an animal of their own or a love of animals | An animal of theirs has fought beside them in 3 of the colony's battles
A great beast tamed | A handler of level 6 or more with a love of animals, where the land has great beasts (huge ones, or as wild as a thrumbo) | One of them is theirs, bonded or as its master

A herd worth the name | Someone who loves animals, the herdmaster, or a keen grower when there's a herd already | The colony's livestock reaches 8 head, or 4 more than when they set out, whichever is more
An animal that knows everything | A handler with a love of animals, with an animal of their own or one going spare | An animal of theirs has learned everything it can be taught
Story | How it starts | How it ends

An old companion | A bonded animal grows old (four fifths of its kind's life) | Quiet hours together, slow afternoons, one more good day. If it dies along the way, its death ends the story, without the usual "came to nothing": a farewell instead.

Raised by hand | A young animal of the colony's loses its mother, and a handler who loves animals, a kind soul, a child or the herdmaster takes it on | Hours at its side and handling practice; once it's grown, the two may bond

The stray | A calm wild animal hangs about the colony and someone leaves scraps out | If it stays a few days, it's marked for taming and the story ends when it's the colony's. If it leaves the land, it's over.
A feud with an animal | Someone else's named animal and a colonist take against each other, often after it stole their food | Open war (a small bad mood), then an uneasy truce, then grudging friends

li.heading: Dilemmas

table.li: Dilemma | When | The choices

The herd or the stores | Food for fewer than 6 days, with a herd of 4 or more eating from the same stores | Cull about a quarter of the herd (1 to 4 head, never the last 2), tighten everyone's belts, turn the weakest out to forage, or let the handler choose. A cull is real: the handlers slaughter the marked animals.
A raider in the crops | Spring to autumn, a wild grazer in or near the fields | Send the hunters, watch the fields at night, try to tame it, or let it eat. The crops it eats are lost.

Medicine for an animal | One of the colony's animals is ill, with 1 to 15 medicine in store | The good medicine, herbs only, its person nursing it through, or nothing. The answer sets its medical care.

Something at the pens | A predator on the land near a herd of 2 or more | Hunt it, keep watch at the pens, bring the herd in close, or leave it be. A predator left alone may break in and take one of the herd.

A bond against the ideoligion | With Ideology: a colonist bonded to an animal, and another whose ideoligion abhors such bonds | Stand by the bond, keep the animal out of the faithful one's way, give it to someone else, or ask for a blessing

Too many in the pens | A herd of 6 grazers or more, the cold that stops the grass within ten days or here, and the hay and kibble in store lasting under three fifths of it | Mark enough for slaughter that the feed lasts (1 to 4, a third of the herd at most: the spare males first, then the oldest, always a male and a female of each kind left, never one carrying young), mark one, or keep them all

What to teach it | One of the colony's grown animals could learn both to guard and to haul and is set to learn neither | Set it to learn to guard (and to go for an enemy) or to haul, the game's own training the handlers then give it; or leave it as it is

li.after: Nobody's own animal, and nothing bonded or named, is ever culled, turned out or lost.

li.heading: The herd's year
li.text:
Three customs can become traditions, like the council's seasonal ones: the lambing watch in spring, when an animal of the herd is in lamb (the whole colony takes turns at the pens through the night), and shearing day in spring or summer, when there are animals to shear or milk (the whole colony at the pens and something to eat in the sun after); both ask for a herd of 2 or more. And bringing the herd home: before the winter (the cold coming in the fall), in a cold snap, or the day after a raid, with a herd of 3 or more, a barn or a pen for it, and 2 or more of it out in the open. It's asked in that moment, after the usual gap between questions. Held, a work party of up to 5 goes out with ropes: each puts a rope on an animal grazing in the open, the game's own way, and walks it into its pen or the barn (handling practice and contentment, no mood). One person can do it alone instead, or the herd can be left to find its own way in, which worries the one who asked. The answer "bring the herd in close" when a predator stalks the pens sends two out the same way.
On the calendar, the colony's first foal is written down the day it's born and kept as a feast, and a beloved animal's day, for a bonded animal that died after a year or more with the colony or fighting for its person, is kept as a remembrance by those who loved it (up to 3).

li.heading: Dreams and setbacks
li.text:
People dream of the herd, of animals that talk, of something at the pens, of riding (children), of a beloved animal grown old, and, after a bonded animal dies, of it coming back.
Two setbacks come from the pens: "one of the herd was taken" (-3 for 4 days) and "the pen was broken into" (-2 for 3 days), when a predator the council left alone, or let close, gets in.

li.heading: The herd's leader and its line
li.text: Once the colony's herd is four head or more, it has a leader: the eldest adult of the kind there is most of, named (if it had no name) by its keeper, the herdmaster, or whoever is best with animals, who speaks to it at the pens. A letter tells it, and the chronicle keeps it. From then on the leader's line is counted: a calf born to the leader is the second generation, its calf the third, and the first calf of each new generation is news. When the leader grows old (four fifths of its kind's years) its last season is told, and the keeper sits with it at the pens of an evening. When it dies, the herd has lost its leader: the keeper takes it hard for a few days, and within a day or two the herd follows a new one, the old leader's own blood first if any is grown, else the eldest of the many, and a new line begins.

li.heading: The first calf of spring
li.text: The first animal born to the herd each spring is a moment: a letter, a small glad thought for everyone, and the keeper walks down to the pens and stays a while until it stands. (The colony's very first foal is still written down on the calendar, as before.)

li.heading: At a glance
li.text: The Overview page's card "The herd and the land" shows who leads the herd, of which line and generation, whether the old leader is in its last season, the beast the colony watches and what it has made of it, any rumour of a shiny Pokémon nearby, and the neighbours settled for good. In development mode, "Rimfolk: check myself" says what stands between the herd and a leader or between a wild animal and a name right now.

li.heading: A beast that stays
li.text: A wild animal of some size that stays on the colony's land three days running, a wolf, a bear, a stag, a boar, not an insect and not a great beast (those have their own stories), is given a name: a child names it, when there is one, else someone with a love of animals, else anyone, and a letter tells the colony. From then on whoever sees it says so, in their own words. Four days after the naming the council is asked what to make of it, and again every eight days while it stays, three times at most. Leave food out for it, and the one who named it carries meat (for a meat-eater) or hay or raw food out to where it is and leaves it; keep everyone close, and the best shot keeps a watch at the gate that night; send the hunters, and the hunters go out after it; let the namer try to tame it, and it goes on the handlers' list; let it be; or drive it off, and two go out at dusk with torches while it makes for the edge of the land. Once the colony has fed it, the colonists talk of it as an animal they feed, whatever else was decided about it. After fifteen days it is part of the land and the story closes, the namer glad of it; hunted, tamed, driven off, dead or moved on, it closes sooner, and the chronicle keeps how. Another beast can take its place twenty days later; one whose story has closed is never taken up again. If it is of a kind your colonists hold sacred, a believer may say whose they take it for when it is named; the council's question about it then has their answer first, to leave it be (they walk out at dusk and stand within sight of it a while), and that is the answer if none is given. Kept a whole season, it is in the colony's book of the gods.

li.heading: Omen animals
li.text:
An animal born to the colony under a sign is an omen. The signs, in this order: an eclipse over its map, an aurora, a shiny Pokémon born or hatched (with PokéWorld), and a day the colony keeps (a tradition, the founding day, a day you named, or one kept before; half the births on such a day). At most one omen in 20 days, and three living at once in a colony. An animal of a kind your colonists hold sacred to a god, born on that god's feast day, is an omen too while there is room among the three, named in that god's own words.
Born, it is news and goes in the chronicle; its keeper (its mother's person, the herdmaster, else whoever is best with animals) names it, half the time with a name the sign gives (Umbra, Glimmer, Gleam, Jubilee), says the name over it when they're by, and writes about it; whoever is with them says something back. While it thrives (alive, up, not ill and not starving), everyone of its colony is a little glad of it (+2, named in the mood). If it dies, it is a bad omen for everyone of its colony (-4 for 5 days), told and remembered in the chronicle. Sold, released or run off, it is simply gone, with no ill luck in it. The setting is "Omen animals" (What's on).

li.heading: Sacred animals
li.text:
With Ideology, the animals the colony's faith holds sacred are the game's venerated animals, and the game's own rules stay: hunting, slaughtering or eating one is wrong for those who hold it so, and a tame one's death is mourned. Rimfolk adds what the game leaves out. One that falls on the colony's land and wasn't the colony's (a wild one, a neighbour's, a manhunter brought down) is grieved by those whose own faith holds it sacred (-2 for 3 days, three at most), with a word over the body and a line in the news. A believer who sees a hunt marked on one says they'll have no part of it. The council's cull never marks one.
From spring to autumn, with one of them on the land, the council may be asked to keep a day for the sacred animals: someone whose faith holds them so carries food out to one of them where it is, and everyone gathers near it for the afternoon (+3 for 3 days for all), or the food is left and the day goes on (+2 for the one who carried it), or not this year. Kept, it is one of the colony's customs: it goes on the calendar, its question comes round on that date each year, and kept three years running it is a tradition. The setting is "Sacred animals" (What's on).

li.heading: Hunting for themselves
li.text:
The game lets a tame animal hunt only when its kind counts as a predator, and only when nothing at all is left to eat, so a dog kept out of the stores goes hungry. With "Pets hunt for themselves" on (What's on), an animal whose kind hunts in real life goes after wild prey below it in the food chain when it is hungry and nothing it may eat lies inside its allowed area. It uses the game's own hunt: it kills, then eats. Two or more of a pack kind (dogs, wolves, hyenas, lions, raptors) beside each other take something a little bigger together.
Now and then, about once in four days, a fed one idle in its area goes after small game, as a cat keeps the mice down. A third of the time, with its person about, it carries the kill to them and sets it at their feet (+3 for 2 days, "a present from my animal"). Whoever sees a kill says a word, and its card says what it caught.
It never sets out while drafted, following its master into work or a fight, roped or penned, with a group, young, under 60% of its health, ill enough for bed, or with danger on the map, and it gives up a chase that takes it 6 cells out of its area. Once it is on the hunt, a bite in the fight or the prey turning on it doesn't make it give up; only being badly hurt, bleeding out, your word or another danger does, and once the prey is dead it eats. The fight is the game's own, so prey fighting back can hurt it now and then, as it hurts the game's wild hunters; the prey it picks keeps that small. Each such animal has a "May hunt" button: off, it stays at home and never hunts, the game's own last resort included.

li.heading: Who hunts, and what

table.li: Kind | Its place | It takes
Husky, labrador, terrier and the other dogs | a hunter (a small dog a small hunter), in packs | hares, squirrels, rats, foxes; two together an ibex
Pug, French bulldog, shih-tzu, chihuahua | prey: bred for company | nothing
Cat, any breed | a small hunter | rats, squirrels, hares, up to a quarter of a man's size
Fox, lynx, weasel, ferret | a small hunter | mice, rats, hares, small birds
Wolf, hyena, coyote | a hunter, in packs | hares and foxes alone; two wolves together an ibex or a gazelle
Bear, cougar, panther, lion, crocodile | apex | a cougar a gazelle or a goat; a bear a deer or a boar
Eagle, hawk, owl, snake, monitor | by its size | small game
Grazers, browsers, fowl, rooters, lizards, apes, fish eaters | prey | nothing

Pokémon | by species and type: canines, foxes, cats, birds of prey, snakes, crocodiles, the hunting dragons, fossils and bugs; an unnamed Dark type of some size or a big Dragon type | an Arcanine a Rattata or a Pidgey, a Growlithe a hare
Any other kind | the game's predator flag, or a meat-only diet with teeth or claws, by its size; else prey | as its place allows

li.after: It takes only wild animals lower than itself, at most four fifths of its size alone (six fifths with another of its kind), weaker and unlikely to turn on it. Never a person, anyone's tame or penned animal, an insect or a venomous animal (a mongoose takes snakes), a herd on the move, an animal marked for taming or left to die for its body, a manhunter, one that bursts when it dies, a sacred or legendary one, or a beast of the colony's stories (a named alpha, a beast nemesis, the beast that stays, a legend). It hunts only inside its allowed area. The dev action "Pets hunting: why an animal hunts or not" writes its place and what it could take now to the log.

li.heading: No food in reach
li.text: An alert, "Animal with no food in reach" (with the alerts, on by default), names the colony's animals that are hungry, have nothing they may eat inside their allowed area and can't hunt for it. It says why for each one: the food it eats lies outside its area, the food inside it is forbidden, or there is nothing it eats on the map; and why it can't hunt: its kind doesn't, its "May hunt" is off, it is too young, there is nothing it could hunt inside its area, or it can't just now. To put it right, set its area to Unrestricted on the Animals tab or widen it, unforbid the food, or put a stockpile of what it eats inside its area. A click selects them, and the one bonded to it says so aloud once. Penned and hitched animals have the game's own alerts.

li.heading: Riding out to far work (with Giddy-Up 2)
li.text:
Giddy-Up decides who may ride what. By its own rules a colonist looks for a mount only when their next job is further away than its setting "Find a mount if trip is longer than" (120 cells by default, about half a large map), measured in a straight line from where they stand, and never while drafted. Most work past the walls is closer than that, so colonists walked out to it and back.
With the setting "Ride out to far work and back" (Your other mods, Giddy-Up 2), Rimfolk adds the trips Giddy-Up leaves out. A free colonist whose next job is 40 cells or more away, where the work, the place a haul goes, or the colonist is 10 cells or more past the home area's edge, first gets on the beast that gets them there soonest. They ride out, leave the beast near the work the way Giddy-Up does (at a mount spot, in a pen, or hitched close by), and ride back on it when they are done there. Going out they ride whenever a beast is free that is no further from them than the work and no slower than they walk, even when the pen lies the other way, since the beast then waits for the way home and every trip after. Coming back they ride when it takes no more than a quarter longer than walking. While they are still at work out there the beast keeps waiting for them: Giddy-Up's "Wait for rider" time runs again from now, looked at every few seconds, until a day after the last job they began. A drafted colonist given a movement order that far rides when riding gets them there sooner, and a handler out past the base sent to lead one of the colony's beasts home rides it to its pen instead. Inside the base nothing changes.

table.li: What decides | How

Giddy-Up's settings | Which kinds of animal can be ridden (bigger than 1.2 body size by default, or the list you set there), "Find a mount if trip is longer than" (120 cells), "Autohitch threshold" (a beast is hitched near the work when no mount spot or pen is within 50 cells of it), "Too injured threshold" (75% health), "Wait for rider timer" (10000 ticks, 4 hours), and whether Ride and Roll (riding to work) and battle mounts (riding while drafted) are on.
The Animals tab | Giddy-Up's automount column: anyone, colonists only, slaves too, or nobody may take this beast.
The Assign tab | Giddy-Up's "allowed to ride" for each colonist. A child too young for handling work, or someone in a wheelchair, never rides.

The beast | Grown, tame, strong enough to carry its rider, not hurt below the threshold or needing a wound tended, not urgently hungry or very tired, and not busy, led on a rope or reserved by someone.

Rimfolk | Never a beast at work (hauling, hunting, fighting), with a group (a caravan, a ritual), with young, carrying a rider, kept for another rider it is waiting for or who is getting on it, or kept for the colony's own post rider. Giddy-Up's mark keeping a beast for someone is left aside when the beast is doing none of that. Going out, never a beast further from them than the work or slower than they walk. A beast someone failed to get on is passed over by them for an hour.
Giddy-Up's areas | Its "forbid riding area" and "mount spots" still say where riders get off.

li.after: Nothing is said aloud and nothing sends a message: they simply ride. In development mode, "Riding out: why a colonist rides or not (log)" writes the colonist's last decision on a trip of 40 cells or more (when, the job, why, the best beast and whether they got on), then for their current job Giddy-Up's settings, the trip and how far past the home area it lies, every one of the colony's beasts with the reason it may or may not be ridden, and Rimfolk's answer. "Rimfolk: check myself" says when riding out is off and why.

li.heading: Waiting for a bleeding animal to die
li.text:
A strong wild animal bleeding from a fight, with a predator or with your own people, can be left to die instead of hunted. Select it and press "Take the body when it dies" (on any bleeding animal that isn't the colony's, wild or another people's). The haul mark shows over it, and nobody goes near it while it lives: the mark takes the place of a hunting or taming order, and the colony's pets leave it alone too. When it dies, of its wounds or anything else, its body is unforbidden and marked for hauling, and a hauler takes it to storage by the usual rules, so a freezer or a stockpile that allows corpses gets it. If no storage on the map takes it, you are told once, and it waits where it fell until one does.
The button's tooltip says how fast it bleeds and, as the health tab does, whether it bleeds to death and about when. The game's wounds stop bleeding on their own after a day and a half to three days (the deeper the wound, the longer), and an animal losing less than a tenth of its blood a day makes it up again, so a lightly hurt one may live. If it stops bleeding (its wounds close with time, someone tends them, or they heal), is tamed, joins the colony or leaves the map, the order is cancelled and a message names it and says why. The game's Cancel tool takes the mark off at any time. The setting is "Take a bleeding animal's body when it dies" (What's on, with the strangers and creatures), and it needs the deeper game hooks.
